why: 0:06 the beige Honeywell cover is pulled straight off; 0:08 the mechanism plate with the round dial is exposed.

edits.say: At the breaker panel, find the breaker that feeds your furnace and flip its plastic toggle to OFF.
placements: breaker feeding the furnace → OFF, flipped with a finger. The video's panel has a handwritten 'Furnace' label at slot 18 (right column), but the hand works a breaker in the left column around slots 7-9, so use your own panel's label

why: 0:16 shows 'Furnace' handwritten next to slot 18 in the right column, but at 0:18 the hand is on a left-column breaker near slots 7-9, so 'the black breaker labelled Furnace on the left side' doesn't match what was flipped. 0:08-0:10 he also checks the live plate with the tester before going to the panel.
0:20-0:26 the orange/yellow pen tester is held to the plate and shows only its green ready light (no voltage alarm) after the breaker is off.
0:30 yellow driver backs out the base screws; 0:32-0:36 the beige base is held away from the wall on red, blue, green and cream wires. The old base shows letters W (top left), Y and G (right side).

0:38 the new white plate is on the wall with the four wires through its top opening; 0:40 a yellow-tipped screwdriver tightens the right mounting screw. The plate is in place by 0:38, slightly before the planned 39 s.

edits.instruction: Move each wire to the terminal with the same letter it used on the old base.
edits.say: Read the letter each wire was on in your photo of the old base. Push that wire into the hole with the same letter on the black strip (B, O, G, Y, W, NOT USED, R, RC from left to right) and tighten its screw.
placements: each wire that was on G, Y or W on the old base → into the hole under the same letter on the black terminal strip (G is 3rd, Y 4th, W 5th from the left), screw tightened with a small screwdriver
red wire (on the top-right screw of the old base) → into the R hole, 7th from the left just before RC; the video doesn't show this insertion, so check the new thermostat's manual for R vs RC

why: 0:44-0:56 is a split-screen comparing the old base letters (W, Y, G) with the new strip 'B O G Y W NOT USED R RC', with arrows on G, Y, W; no wire is ever shown going in. The wires are blue, green, red and cream. There is no yellow or white wire, so 'white into W, yellow into Y' is invented.

edits.say: Flip the same breaker back to ON. Snap the thermostat onto the plate and check that its screen lights up with the room temperature.
placements: the same breaker you switched off → ON, flipped with a finger (in the video, a left-column breaker around slot 9)
white rectangular Honeywell Home thermostat body → snapped onto the white wall plate centered on the white wall, screen facing out

why: 0:58 a finger on a left-column breaker near slot 9 (not the slot-18 'Furnace' label); 1:00 the Honeywell Home screen reads 89 (room temperature); 1:02-1:04 the furnace is shown. '89' is that room's reading and can't be an instruction for the learner.
